quizzes.title: Sino-Indian Border: States, UTs and Sectors
quizzes.passage: India and China share a long frontier that runs along the Himalayan range. Much of this frontier is not a settled international boundary, and the working line between the two sides is called the Line of Actual Control. It is described as an effective military border that separates Indian-controlled areas from those held by China. Officials describe the LAC as a practical boundary rather than a legally recognised one. The frontier passes through several Indian states and one Union Territory, and each stretch has its own terrain and local conditions. India administers Arunachal Pradesh as a full-fledged state with established government institutions and civil administration. For management purposes, the LAC is divided into sectors so that officials can focus on a defined stretch. In 1954, India and China signed the Panchsheel Agreement, and its principles included a pledge by both sides to respect each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity. The slogan Hindi-Chini Bhai Bhai captured the mood of mutual trust at that time. The LAC took its practical shape after the 1962 Sino-Indian War, when a ceasefire left each side in control of different areas. Since then, both countries have used a range of mechanisms to manage incidents along the line while the wider question remains open.

questions.q: Which Union Territory shares a border with China?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Ladakh as the one Union Territory that shares the border with China.

questions.q: Sikkim borders China along with which two other countries?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Nepal and Bhutan as the other neighbours of Sikkim, apart from China.

questions.q: Which of these states borders China and forms part of the Middle Sector of the LAC?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh borders China and is part of the Middle Sector, which also covers Uttarakhand.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Ladakh shares the longest border segment with China among all Indian states and UTs.
Reason (R): Ladakh borders Xinjiang Province of China.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the booklet does not present the Xinjiang border as the reason for the length of the segment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's border with China:
I. The border runs through one Union Territory and four states.
II. Arunachal Pradesh shares the longest border segment with China.
III. The Panchsheel Agreement was signed by Nehru and Zhou Enlai.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because Ladakh has the longest segment and Arunachal Pradesh has the second longest.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Arunachal Pradesh borders Myanmar.
II. Uttarakhand borders China and Nepal.
III. Himachal Pradesh forms part of the Eastern Sector.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while Himachal Pradesh is in the Middle Sector, not the Eastern Sector.

questions.q: What name does China use for the part of Arunachal Pradesh that it claims?
questions.explanation: The booklet says China claims part of Arunachal Pradesh as South Tibet.

quizzes.title: Sino-Indian Border: States, UTs and Sectors
quizzes.passage: The boundary between India and China follows the high Himalayan range, and much of it has not been settled by a final agreement. On the ground, the working line between the two sides is known as the Line of Actual Control. This line is described as a practical boundary, not one that is legally recognised as an international border. It is also described as an effective military border that separates the two sides' controlled areas. The frontier cuts through several Indian states and one Union Territory, and each stretch faces its own terrain and local conditions. Earlier, both countries agreed to principles that committed each side to respect the other's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Their relationship was also marked by a slogan of brotherhood that captured a period of mutual trust. After the 1962 conflict, the Line of Actual Control took its practical form as a ceasefire line. Its status has been a source of repeated tension, including clashes between troops in recent years. For management purposes, the line is divided into sectors so that officials can coordinate their work. Today, both sides manage the frontier through a set of mechanisms that respond to incidents, while the wider boundary question remains unresolved.

questions.q: Which Indian state borders China, Nepal and Bhutan? (name the state)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Sikkim as bordering China, Nepal and Bhutan.

questions.q: China refers to part of an Indian state it claims as 'South Tibet'. Which Indian state is this? (name the state)
questions.explanation: The booklet says China claims part of Arunachal Pradesh as South Tibet.

questions.q: Which Indian Union Territory shares a border with China? (name the UT)
questions.explanation: Ladakh is the one Union Territory that borders China, according to the booklet.

questions.q: Which Indian Prime Minister signed the Panchsheel Agreement with China? (name)
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru signed the Panchsheel Agreement with Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai.

questions.q: In which year was the Panchsheel Agreement signed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Panchsheel Agreement to 1954.

questions.q: Which sector of the LAC covers Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh? (name the sector)
questions.explanation: The Middle Sector of the LAC covers Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Which Indian state is surrounded by Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Haryana and Punjab? (name the state)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Himachal Pradesh is surrounded by Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Haryana and Punjab.

quizzes.title: Border Management Mechanisms and Agreements
quizzes.passage: India and China have not reached a final settlement of their boundary dispute, which covers a frontier of 3,488 km along the Himalayan range. Instead, the two sides manage the Line of Actual Control through a layered set of meetings and agreements. Those meetings take place at several levels, from senior government representatives to local officers who work along the line. Military officers also take part in talks when tensions rise, and their discussions are aimed at calming the situation on the ground. Several agreements were signed from the 1990s onward, adding further rules to the arrangement. A later agreement aimed to strengthen communication between the border forces of the two countries. The arrangement has grown over several decades, and each step has added a channel or a rule rather than settling the question. The frontier is also divided into sectors for management purposes, so that each stretch can be discussed separately. The line itself is a practical boundary rather than a legally recognised international border, so these arrangements matter for daily management. Because the frontier is long and varied, managing it is a continuing task. Together, these tools help keep the frontier calm while the wider dispute remains open.

questions.q: Which mechanism is the highest political-level channel for pursuing a final political settlement of the boundary dispute?
options: Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination
questions.explanation: The Special Representatives on Boundary Question, set up in 2003, is the highest political-level mechanism for a final settlement.

questions.q: Which mechanism, set up in 2012, is a diplomatic and military channel for LAC incidents and has no mandate to settle the boundary?
options: Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination
questions.explanation: The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination handles LAC incidents but has no mandate to settle the boundary.

questions.q: Which agreement restricted military activities and the use of weapons near the LAC?
options: 1993 Agreement for Maintenance of Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC
questions.explanation: The 1996 Confidence-Building Measures Agreement restricted military activities and the use of weapons near the LAC.

questions.q: Which mechanism pursues tactical disengagement, de-escalation and buffer-zone arrangements during major standoffs?
options: Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination
questions.explanation: Corps Commander-level Meetings are the high-level military negotiations used for tactical disengagement and buffer-zone arrangements.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination has the mandate to settle the boundary dispute.
Reason (R): The Working Mechanism coordinates diplomatic and military responses to LAC incidents.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Working Mechanism has no mandate to settle the boundary, although it does coordinate responses to LAC incidents.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 1993 agreement recognised the LAC and committed both sides to maintaining peace.
II. The 2005 CBM Protocol set procedures for face-to-face encounters between troops.
III. The Special Representatives mechanism was set up in 1993.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the Special Representatives mechanism was set up in 2003, not 1993.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Border Personnel Meeting Points are designated locations where local military commanders address ground-level friction.
II. The 1996 Confidence-Building Measures agreement was signed during Chinese President Jiang Zemin's visit to India.
III. The Working Mechanism was set up in 2003.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while the Working Mechanism was set up in 2012, not 2003.

quizzes.title: Border Management Mechanisms and Agreements
quizzes.passage: The India-China boundary remains unresolved, and the two countries handle the frontier through a set of mechanisms rather than a single settlement. The line runs for 3,488 km along the Himalayan range. Some arrangements are led by senior officials who discuss the long-term question, while others help deal with incidents. Local military commanders have a role at specific points on the ground, where they can meet to talk through friction. At higher levels, talks have been used when standoffs grow serious, to plan steps that reduce tension. Several agreements were concluded over the years, adding rules on the conduct of troops and on military activity near the line. The arrangement has grown over several decades, and each step has added a channel or a rule rather than settling the question. The frontier is also divided into sectors for management purposes, so that each stretch can be discussed separately. The line itself is a practical boundary rather than a legally recognised international border, so these arrangements matter for daily management. Because the frontier is long and varied, managing it is a continuing task for officials on both sides. Together, they show that the dispute is being managed even though it is still pending.

questions.q: Which Chinese President visited India in 1996, when a confidence-building agreement was signed? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 1996 Confidence-Building Measures agreement was signed during Chinese President Jiang Zemin's visit to India.

questions.q: Which Indian Prime Minister was visiting China when the 1993 agreement on peace and tranquillity was signed? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says PM Narasimha Rao was visiting China when the 1993 agreement was signed.

questions.q: In which year was the Special Representatives mechanism set up? (year)
questions.explanation: The Special Representatives on Boundary Question mechanism was set up in 2003.

questions.q: In which year was the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination set up? (year)
questions.explanation: The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination was set up in 2012.

questions.q: What are the designated locations where local military commanders meet to address ground-level friction called? (name in full)
questions.explanation: Border Personnel Meeting Points are the designated locations where local commanders meet to address ground-level friction.

questions.q: Which 2005 protocol set procedures for face-to-face encounters between troops? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The 2005 CBM Protocol set procedures for face-to-face encounters between troops.

questions.q: Which 2013 agreement strengthened communication and coordination between border forces? (give the acronym)
questions.explanation: The 2013 Border Defence Cooperation Agreement, abbreviated BDCA, strengthened communication and coordination between border forces.
